cards.definition: Resistance or objections to a proposal.
cards.example:
- We got some pushback from legal, but the argument was reasonable.
Tivemos alguma resistência do jurídico, mas o argumento era razoável.
cards.note: Verbo separado: push back on something. Substantivo junto: pushback.

cards.definition: Agreement between people or teams on what to do.
cards.example:
- Before the board meeting, I need alignment between sales and product.
Antes da reunião do conselho, preciso de alinhamento entre vendas e produto.
cards.note: Verbo align. Get alignment on = alinhar sobre.

cards.definition: The limits of what a project includes.
cards.example:
- That request is outside the scope of this quarter's project.
Aquele pedido está fora do escopo do projeto deste trimestre.
cards.note: Scope creep = escopo que cresce sem controle — termo de gestão de projetos.

cards.definition: To use something you already have to get an advantage.
cards.example:
- We can leverage last year's data to justify the investment.
Podemos alavancar os dados do ano passado para justificar o investimento.
cards.note: Verbo e substantivo; soa estratégico em reunião executiva.

cards.definition: Answerable for a result, not only for the tasks.
cards.example:
- I'm accountable for the result, not just for the tasks.
Eu respondo pelo resultado, não só pelas tarefas.
cards.note: Mais forte que responsible: implica prestar contas. -able final soa como “-a-bou”, quase engolido.

cards.definition: To make a risk or a problem less serious.
cards.example:
- We can mitigate the risk with a two-week pilot.
Podemos mitigar o risco com um piloto de duas semanas.
cards.note: Colocação padrão: mitigate a risk. Substantivo: mitigation.

cards.definition: A professional way of questioning what was just said.
cards.example:
- I'd like to challenge that assumption, if I may — the data suggests otherwise.
Eu gostaria de questionar essa premissa, se me permite — os dados sugerem o contrário.
cards.note: Discordar de alguém sênior sem confronto: questiona a IDEIA, não a pessoa.

cards.translation: vamos deixar isso de lado por ora
cards.definition: Used to postpone a subject without rejecting it.
cards.example:
- Good point — let's park that and come back to it after the numbers.
Bom ponto — vamos deixar isso de lado e voltar depois dos números.
cards.note: Controla a pauta sem descartar a contribuição de ninguém.

cards.definition: Final; the one that happens in the end.
cards.example:
- The eventual decision was to postpone the launch by one quarter.
A decisão final foi adiar o lançamento em um trimestre.
cards.note: “Eventual” em português = ocasional; em inglês eventual = FINAL. Erro que passa batido até em C1.

cards.definition: To consist of; to be made up of.
cards.example:
- The board comprises seven members from four countries.
O conselho é composto por sete membros de quatro países.
cards.note: “Comprometer-se” é commit; “comprometer” no sentido de pôr em risco é jeopardize. Compromise é o meio-termo (substantivo) e só combina com security, quality, safety. Comprise = ser formado por: “The board comprises five members.” s soa como Z.

questions.prompt: We got some _____ from legal, but the argument was reasonable.
questions.explanation: “Pushback FROM” the people resisting. It is uncountable: some pushback.

questions.prompt: Before the board meeting, I need _____ between sales and product.
That request is outside the _____ of this quarter's project.
questions.explanation: “Outside the scope” is the standard way to refuse extra work politely.

options: We can leverage last year's data.
We can leverage on last year's data.
We can leverage of last year's data.
We can leverage with last year's data.
questions.answer: We can leverage last year's data.
questions.explanation: As a verb, “leverage” takes the object directly.
“Accountable FOR” a result, “accountable TO” a person. Portuguese “por” tempts “by”.

questions.prompt: A gente consegue reduzir o risco com um piloto de duas semanas.
questions.answer: We can mitigate the risk with a two-week pilot.|We can mitigate the risk with a two week pilot.
questions.explanation: “Mitigate” is to reduce the seriousness of a risk.

questions.prompt: _____ — the numbers from March point the other way.
questions.explanation: Questions the claim without attacking the person.

questions.prompt: Good point, but _____ and come back to it after the budget.
questions.explanation: Postpones a subject without rejecting it.

options: The eventual decision took three months.
We have eventual meetings on Fridays.
She is eventual in the office.
questions.answer: The eventual decision took three months.

questions.prompt: The team has four analysts and one manager. The team…
questions.explanation: “Comprise” takes the object directly — no “of”. And it is not the Portuguese “compreender” (to understand).
